## Intent
Hypothesis: Halide-expressible math (walk1) with identity ordering and no intermediates compiles to vectorized code approaching the streaming bandwidth ceiling.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill at N≈963 falls below the smallest measured point (N=4000), so only the L2-resident and DRAM regimes are observed. At q=0.01, ns/p falls from 12.219 at N=4000 to 8.538 at N=16000 — overhead amortization. The L2→DRAM spill at N≈61680 sits between N=16000 and N=65000; crossing it produces no knee: ns/p goes 8.538→8.343→8.373 across N=16000/65000/262000, then rises gently to 8.78 at N=4M. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: the flat region sits at ~8.3 ns/p (q=0.01), ~9.0 (q=0.05), and ~11.3 (q=0.25), each showing the same amortize-then-flatten profile. The absence of any spill knee confirms the bottleneck is not cache capacity.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.15 GB/s at N=65000, q=0.01 — 32.3% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. At q=0.05 the peak is 7.53 GB/s (29.9%); at q=0.25, 6.03 GB/s (23.9%). The algo is compute/overhead-bound: bandwidth is flat across N from 16000 onward at every death rate, and never exceeds a third of ceiling. Death rate monotonically erodes throughput — roughly 2.1 GB/s lost from q=0.01 to q=0.25 — as branchy respawn cost accumulates.

## Assembly
No vectorization — zero vector-suffixed instructions in 345 insns. All FP is scalar: `fmul` (×4), `fadd` (×1), `fsub` (×1), `fcvtzs` (×5) on `s` registers. Particle loads use scalar pairs `ldp s5, s6` and `ldp s7, s16`, not vector loads. The Halide math is a non-inlined call: `bl _halide_b2_math`. The pixel scatter is byte-granular RMW: `ldrb w2, [x1]` → `add` → `csel` (saturate to 0xff) → `strb w2, [x1]`, repeated per channel. The 21 branches, 20 `cmp`, 18 `csel`, and 6 `ccmp` per step confirm heavily branchy scalar codegen, explaining why throughput stalls at 32% of ceiling — the byte-granular scatter and absent SIMD cap it far below streaming.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo peaks at 8.15 GB/s (32% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) with zero vector instructions and a non-inlined `bl _halide_b2_math` call, so Halide-expressible math did not compile to streaming-efficient code. Death rate worsens it to 6.03 GB/s (24%) at q=0.25, but even at q=0.01 the 3× gap from ceiling refutes the hypothesis.
